rationale: The English cue and both translations identify the same automotive device, but the national distinction is materially overstated. Malaysian authoritative terminology uses "pengelap cermin depan", while Malaysian automotive usage also uses the borrowing "wiper"; Indonesian automotive usage likewise uses "wiper" alongside native equivalents such as "penyeka kaca". The forms are reasonable variety-associated preferences, not reliably different common words. The blank contrast also fails to explain the overlap or establish a genuine false-friend distinction.
